walkthroughs.body_html:
Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours.

The side facing the Sun has day. The side facing away has night.

The Sun doesn't move across the sky - we do. The Sun appears to rise in the east because Earth spins from west to east.

While Earth spins, it also orbits the Sun.

One orbit takes about 365.25 days - one year.

The quarter-day adds up, so every 4 years we add a leap day (29th February) to catch up.

Earth's orbit is a slightly squashed circle called an ellipse.

The Moon doesn't make its own light - it reflects sunlight.

As the Moon orbits Earth (~28 days), we see different fractions lit up:

New Moon -> First Quarter -> Full Moon -> Last Quarter -> repeat.

The Moon hasn't changed - just our view of it from Earth.

Spins on its axis
Wobbles in space
The Sun turns off at night

It's a small star

mcqs.q: When you rub a balloon and stick it to the wall, what has been transferred?
options: Protons jumped from the balloon to the wall, causing static cling.
Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
Electrons have been transferred between the balloon and the cloth (not the wall).
The galaxies are turning red because they are getting older.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies indicate?
options: Galaxies are moving through space away from us, like objects flying outward from a centre.
The galaxies are turning red because they are getting older.
Space itself is expanding, stretching the wavelength of light from distant galaxies as it travels.

options: In practice, no — some energy is always transferred to less useful stores (e.g. heat to surroundings).
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
A well-designed device can be 100 percent efficient by eliminating all friction.
